To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel Latent Causal Invariance Model (LaCIM), which is a causal prediction framework that can avoid spurious correlation.
we introduce a latent variable framework for learning causal factors, and show its utility in terms of interpretability, out of distribution generalization and robustness.

(a) we propose a novel causal inference framework for learning spurious-free representations, (b) we prove that the proposed framework is identifiable and can be used for prediction and robustness, (c) we show that the proposed framework can be used for various applications, including healthcare and security.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects: 1) the causal inference problem in machine learning, 2) the disentangled representation learning problem, and 3) the robust learning and prediction problem.
the following three questions: (1) How can we avoid spurious correlation in learning from data? (2) How can we make the model more interpretable?
the problem of learning a latent variable model that can disentangle the causal structure and avoid spurious correlation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we introduce the concept of \emph{latent causal invariant model}, which is a novel framework for causal inference, and we provide a theoretical guarantee that it can disentangle the causal factors from the confounding factors, which is crucial to interpret the causal factors.
our approach is able to achieve better interpretability, out of distribution generalization, robustness and security, compared to the baselines.
our proposed LaCIM is able to achieve causal prediction by disentangling the latent factors, which is a key for improving the interpretability, OOD generalization and robustness of deep learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we propose a latent space model to learn the causal structure of the data, and then perform prediction in the latent space to obtain causal prediction.
, we propose a latent causal invariant model for learning causal prediction and disentanglement.
, we propose a novel latent variable model that is theoretically guaranteed to disentangle the underlying causal factors from confounders and thus can avoid spurious correlation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
causal prediction is more robust and interpretable than data fitting.
the latent space of a causal model is a natural space for causal prediction.
\textbf{\emph{causes are the key to understanding and prediction}}, and the causal invariance assumption is a useful tool for learning causal models from data.
